newsitem.title: USA: Republican narrowly wins Connecticut House seat.
newsitem.headline: Republican narrowly wins Connecticut House seat.

text.p: Representative Nancy Johnson, hammered by her opponent as a clone of unpopular House speaker Newt Gingrich, was belatedly declared the winner Thursday in an extremely close congressional race.
Republican Johnson, a seven-term incumbent from Connecticut's 6th Congressional District, is also chairman of the House Ethics Committee, which has been investigating Gingrich's finances.

She defeated Democrat Charlotte Koskoff by only 1,587 votes in a district where almost 228,000 votes were cast, according to final tabulations by Connecticut's Secretary of State. A threshold of 1,138 votes or less would have required an automatic recount.

Koskoff campaigned on a consistent message that a vote for Johnson was a vote for Gingrich and the "Contract with America" he co-authored. Koskoff also attacked Johnson for her leadership of the Ethics Committee, which has been slow to respond to charges that Gingrich improperly mixed politics and a taxpayer-supported college course he taught.
Johnson said her role on the committee "absolutely hurt me" in the election, the Hartford Courant reported Thursday.

In 1994, she called Gingrich "one of the most visionary thinkers in American politics" when she seconded his nomination for speaker. But Johnson, in Congress since 1982, insisted that Koskoff had distorted her record in a negative campaign.
